text: When Tom asked who he was the stranger said that he went by many names. <break time="0.8s" /> And Tom realized. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was talking to Old Scratch. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Meeting such a figure. <break time="0.8s" /> Would have frightened most men. <break time="0.8s" /> But Tom had lived so long with a fierce wife. <break time="0.8s" /> That he did not fear even the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Scratch offered him Kidds treasure. <break time="0.8s" /> On certain conditions. <break time="0.8s" /> Which must have been hard. <break time="0.8s" /> Since Tom asked for time to think them over. <break time="0.8s" /> As proof the devil pressed a finger on Toms forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Tom got home. <break time="0.8s" /> He found a black fingerprint. <break time="0.8s" /> Burned into his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom told his wife the whole secret. <break time="0.8s" /> And she, greedy for the hidden gold. <break time="0.8s" /> Urged him to accept the bargain at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of pure stubbornness Tom refused. <break time="0.8s" /> So she decided to make the deal herself. <break time="0.8s" /> And keep all the gold for herself. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening she set off for the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> With the silver teapot and spoons. <break time="0.8s" /> Tied up in her apron. <break time="0.8s" /> And she never came back. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for her at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom found her apron hanging in a tree. <break time="0.8s" /> And the ground below was trampled. <break time="0.8s" /> As if by a fierce struggle. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing clumps of black hair there. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom guessed that she had fought the devil hard. <break time="0.8s" /> And the loss of his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Made up for the loss of his silver.
